podcast.title: Co-Credit for Elvis
podcast.body: Otis Blackwell was credited as co-writer for "Don't Be Cruel" alongside Elvis Presley, at the insistence of Colonel Tom Parker, who wanted Elvis to "get a cut for making it a hit." "Don't be cruel, a song written by Otis Blackwell, but credited to Blackwell and Presley, as the Colonel insisted that his boy get a cut for making it a hit."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Professional Songwriter
podcast.body: Otis Blackwell was a New York-based songwriter, one of a relatively small number of black people who successfully secured work as a professional songwriter for major publishing companies. "He was a New York-based songwriter, one of a relatively small number of black people, who managed to get work as a professional songwriter for one of the big publishing companies."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Superstition about Meeting Elvis
podcast.body: Otis Blackwell intentionally never met Elvis Presley, even declining an opportunity, because he developed a superstition about meeting the artist who had given him his biggest hits. "The one time he did have a chance to meet him, he declined, as he developed a superstition about meeting the man who'd given him his biggest hits."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
